prompt:
Reports from support and security about alerts and the inbox:

1. Security: any member can open another member's inbox by changing the address, and can mark another member's alerts as read. Changing another member's notification settings works too.
2. "Mark all read" in one person's inbox clears the unread alerts of everyone else in the workspace.
3. Clicking an alert about an issue opens a page that does not exist. The links in search results and in the daily digest are broken the same way, and the alert about a new member leads nowhere either.
4. Since a recent change, owners are no longer told when someone joins the workspace; the person who joined gets an alert about themselves instead.
5. Assignees are not told when someone else moves their issue to another status, on the board or otherwise.
6. Someone assigned at the moment an issue is created gets no assignment alert; they only get one when assigned later.
7. When the workspace runs out of room on its plan — a project, a seat, an issue, an upload or a webhook endpoint refused — the owner never hears about it.
8. Alerts a member switched off for the inbox still show up there.

Expected behaviour:

- Inboxes and notification settings are personal: a member reads, marks read and configures only their own, whatever their role; anyone else's are refused. Marking all read marks that member's own unread alerts and nothing else. An inbox lists exactly the alerts delivered to it in-app, however many, with no entry duplicated or missing across pages; an alert the member switched off for in-app never appears there, whatever other channels it goes to.
- Every alert and every search hit links to the page the app actually serves. An alert about an issue (assignment, status change, overdue reminder, comment, mention), a search hit for an issue and a search hit for a comment all link to that issue's page in its workspace and project; a search hit for a project links to the project's page; the alert about a new member links to the members settings page; the alert about a full plan links to the billing settings page. Digest entries carry the same links as the alerts they summarise.
- The workspace owner is told when a new member joins; the person who joined is not told about themselves.
- The assignee of an issue is told when somebody else changes its status, including by moving it on the board; nobody is told about their own change, and nothing is sent for an issue that has no assignee. Being assigned at creation is an assignment: the assignee is told exactly as if assigned later, unless they created the issue themselves.
- When a write is refused because the plan has no room for it — another project, another seat (an invitation), another issue in a project, another upload, another webhook endpoint — the workspace owner is told, whoever tried. While that alert is still unread, further refusals for the same resource add nothing; once it has been read, the next refusal produces a new alert. Refusals for different resources are separate alerts. The periodic usage recount, which refuses nothing, never produces one.

This is a `fix` task: edit the code and stop. Do not write a summary and do not emit an ANSWER line.
notes: Injected 2 defects in 2 layers (bug.patch, repository + fan-out): (a) notification-repository markAllRead drops its recipient predicate (comment: the recipient column only routes the bell), so one member's "mark all read" clears the whole organization's unread rows; (b) the member.joined fan-out notifies the person who joined (actorId null) instead of the owner (comment: the welcome goes to the person who joined). Latent in pristine and described by the prompt: notification:read sits at viewer rank in the role matrix, so the recipientId on the resource never matters and any member lists any inbox; markRead updates by notification id without the recipient; updatePreference accepts any userId; every alert href is hand-built (/issues/<id>, /settings/members) although lib/url already has issuePath/projectPath/settingsPath, and search-service's hrefFor builds /issues, /comments and /projects paths the app does not serve (the digest reuses the stored href); no fan-out for issue.status_changed; an issue created with an assignee emits issue.created only, so nobody is told; billing.limit_exceeded is emitted by assertWithinLimit, which no write path calls, and by the usage recount at 90% of a quota, while the five quota guards (createIssue, createProject, inviteMembers, addAttachment, createWebhook) throw without announcing anything, and there is no plan_limit_reached fan-out; listNotifications returns rows regardless of their channels, so an email-only row shows in the inbox. Reference fix (13 source files + 1 visible test, 294 changed lines across types, repositories, services and jobs): a new link-service resolves ids to issuePath/projectPath/settingsPath through the repositories; types/event gives billing.limit_exceeded a trigger (write_refused | usage_rollup); billing-service gains reportLimitReached, which the five guards and assertWithinLimit call; usage-service tags its recount events usage_rollup; notification-repository filters the inbox to rows carrying the in_app channel, scopes markRead to the recipient, restores the recipient on markAllRead and adds hasUnread for de-duplication; notification-service refuses another member's inbox or preferences explicitly (the matrix cannot express "only the recipient"), links every alert through the link-service, alerts the assignee on issue.status_changed by somebody else, treats issue.created with an assignee as an assignment, sends member.joined to the owner, and alerts the owner on write_refused events once per resource while unread; search-service links hits through the link-service; the digest job passes the recipient to markRead; two visible inbox reads that crossed recipients now use the recipient's own actor. Why hard: eight symptoms spread over repositories, three services, the search service, the digest job and the event contract; the inbox privacy cannot be fixed in the role matrix (viewer rank grants everyone); the links must come from one shared resolver because the fan-out, the search service and the digest all produce them; the plan-limit alert needs an event from every refusing guard (none emits today) and must tell a refusal apart from the recount, which emits the same event at 90% without refusing anything; and the alert must survive replay (repeated refusals, the same resource, a different resource) without a schema change. Traps: wrong place (naive B, links fixed in the fan-out only: fails the search-hit case); second entry points (naive C, the limit event emitted from the two guards the report leads with, projects and seats: fails issues, storage and webhooks); second cause (naive D, the owner alert keyed on the event alone so the usage recount alerts too: fails "the periodic recount says nothing"); replay (naive E, no de-duplication: fails "does not repeat while unread"); second entry point for assignment (naive F, issue.created with an assignee not treated as an assignment: fails 6 cases). Hidden test: 24 cases, fake Date pinned to 2026-05-04T08:00Z, real id generator, logger and rate limiter, throwaway database built through the repositories, every quota exercised on a free or growth plan through the real services.
